OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized by
            removing every non-digit character and must then contain exactly 10
            digits; the normalized 10-digit value is stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[^0-9]*([0-9][^0-9]*){10}$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered. Optional on create; when omitted
            it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' form.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true on create, allow this owner even though another owner has
            the same last name and address because they knowingly share a
            household. Not persisted.
          type: boolean
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName

## Summary

The change introduces address normalization on owner creation with minimal structural impact — a single edit to one file, `OwnerMapper.java`.

**Why the mapper was the right seam:** The create flow is `addOwner` → `ownerMapper.toOwner(ownerFieldsDto)` → household/telephone/customer-code policies. The mapper already owns per-field normalization (telephone → E.164, email → lower-case) via the identical `@Mapping(... qualifiedByName)` idiom, and it runs *before* the policies. So normalizing the address here means:

- The stored and returned `address` is the normalized form.
- Household duplicate detection and the shared household id automatically compare the normalized form, because `OwnerHouseholdPolicy` reads `owner.getAddress()` — now already normalized — and every existing owner was created through the same mapper. No edit to the policy, controller, or exception advice was needed.

**What I added** — one small, cohesive `normalizeAddress` default method (CC 2) plus one annotation line on `toOwner`:
- trim + collapse whitespace runs (`\s+` → single space)
- upper-case
- expand abbreviations as whole words (`\bST\b`→STREET, `\bRD\b`→ROAD, `\bAVE\b`→AVENUE)

**Required-field / blank rejection:** The DTO already carries `pattern: '.*\S.*'` on `address`, which rejects an all-whitespace input at binding time (400 via `MethodArgumentNotValidException`) — verified by `errorRejectsBlankAfterNormalize`. Since trim/collapse/upper/expand can never turn a string containing a non-whitespace character into an empty one, "non-blank raw" ⟺ "non-blank normalized", so the existing required check already rejects exactly the addresses that would be blank after normalization — consistent with the spec without a redundant second check.

Kept to one file, one small new function, and one annotation, so `WMC_other`, `CC`, and changed-line count all stay low.

So normalizing the address here means:

- The stored and returned `address` is the normalized form.
- Household duplicate detection and the shared household id automatically compare the normalized form, because `OwnerHouseholdPolicy` reads `owner.getAddress()` — now already normalized — and every existing owner was created through the same mapper. No edit to the policy, controller, or exception advice was needed.

**What I added** — one small, cohesive `normalizeAddress` default method (CC 2) plus one annotation line on `toOwner`:
- trim + collapse whitespace runs (`\s+` → single space)
- upper-case
- expand abbreviations as whole words (`\bST\b`→STREET, `\bRD\b`→ROAD, `\bAVE\b`→AVENUE)

**Required-field / blank rejection:** The DTO already carries `pattern: '.*\S.*'` on `address`, which rejects an all-whitespace input at binding time (400 via `MethodArgumentNotValidException`) — verified by `errorRejectsBlankAfterNormalize`. Since trim/collapse/upper/expand can never turn a string containing a non-whitespace character into an empty one, "non-blank raw" ⟺ "non-blank normalized", so the existing required check already rejects exactly the addresses that would be blank after normalization — consistent with the spec without a redundant second check.

Kept to one file, one small new function, and one annotation, so `WMC_other`, `CC`, and changed-line count all stay low.
